---
title: Case types
description: Workspace-level taxonomy for cases — keys, labels, hierarchy rules, optional fields on each kind of work.
---

A **case type** is the shape of a piece of work: which icon and color appear on the board, whether it allows child cases, and any extra typed fields collectors must fill in. Definitions live in a **singleton** YAML file checked into the workspace repo:

- `.kiket/case_types.yaml` — one top-level `case_types:` array; you can optionally set `model_version` for your own bookkeeping.

Everything under `.kiket/` is file-backed truth: the modeling cockpit edits the same YAML your IDE commits.

## Minimum file

```yaml
case_types:
  - key: control_review
    label: Control review
    allow_children: false
    icon: shield-check
    color: indigo
    position: 0
    active: true
  - key: evidence_gap
    label: Evidence gap
    allow_children: false
    icon: file-warning
    color: amber
    position: 1
    active: true
```

Use **snake_case** field names (`allow_children`, `parent_types`) so the file stays consistent with scaffolded repos and upstream templates.

## Custom fields per type

Each entry can optionally declare typed fields stored on cases of that kind (keys mirror [intake form field vocabulary](/docs/build/intake-forms#field-types) where overlaps exist):

```yaml
case_types:
  - key: contract
    label: Contract review
    allow_children: false
    position: 0
    active: true
    fields:
      - key: counterparty
        label: Counterparty
        type: text
        required: true
      - key: total_value_usd
        label: Total value (USD)
        type: number
```

## Parent / child rules

Hierarchy is controlled with `allow_children` and `parent_types`:

```yaml
case_types:
  - key: epic
    label: Epic
    allow_children: true
    position: 0
    active: true

  - key: story
    label: Story
    allow_children: false
    parent_types: [epic]
    position: 1
    active: true
```

The platform enforces these relationships when creating or linking cases.

## Icon + color

Icons reference the [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) set. Color values are typically tone tokens from your template (for example `danger`, `primary`, `info`) that the board and cards map to theme styles.

## Editing surfaces

Open `.kiket/case_types.yaml` in the **Project editor** modeling tree to use the visual case-type editor, or edit the YAML directly — both write the same file.
